rng.title: How rand::rng works
rng.description: The thread-local random generator: fast, seeded from the OS, ready to use.

note.text: one per thread, cheap to call

slides.caption: rand::rng() returns a handle to a generator that each thread creates on first use and reseeds from time to time.
The first call seeds it from the operating system.
You get a handle; call random(), random_range()... on it.

random.title: How rand::random works
random.description: A random value of any type that supports it, from the thread generator.

slides.caption: Floats are in [0, 1); integers cover their whole range; bool is 50/50.
For many values, keep an rng instead.

random-range-fn.title: How rand::random_range works
random-range-fn.description: A random number in a range, from the thread generator.

slides.caption: Every number in the range is equally likely. ..= includes the end; .. excludes it.
One of them is picked uniformly.

note.text: result: p = 0: always false, p = 1: always true

slides.caption: true if it is the lucky one.

fill-fn.title: How rand::fill works
fill-fn.description: Fills a buffer with random bytes (or numbers).

slides.caption: Uses the thread generator. Not for keys or passwords: use getrandom or a CSPRNG crate.
RngExt::fill does the same with your rng.

rng-random.title: How RngExt::random works
rng-random.description: A random value of the requested type, from your generator.

rng-random-range.title: How RngExt::random_range works
rng-random-range.description: A random number in a range, from your generator.

slides.caption: Works for integers, floats and chars. The result is unbiased: every value is equally likely.

rng-random-bool.title: How RngExt::random_bool works
rng-random-bool.description: true with probability p, from your generator.

rng-random-ratio.title: How RngExt::random_ratio works
rng-random-ratio.description: true with probability n / d, from your generator.

rng-random-iter.title: How RngExt::random_iter works
rng-random-iter.description: An endless iterator of random values.

slides.caption: Take as many as you need.
sample_iter does this for a distribution.

rng-sample.title: How RngExt::sample works
rng-sample.description: Draws one value from a distribution.

slides.caption: Build a Uniform once when drawing many values.

rng-sample-iter.title: How RngExt::sample_iter works
rng-sample-iter.description: An endless iterator of values from a distribution.

slides.caption: Alphanumeric yields bytes from A-Z, a-z and 0-9.
Turn them into chars and collect a String.
For passwords or tokens that must be secret, use a cryptographic generator.

rng-fill.title: How RngExt::fill works
rng-fill.description: Fills a slice with random values from your generator.

slides.caption: Faster than filling one by one.

choose.title: How IndexedRandom::choose works
choose.description: Picks one random element of a slice, or None if it is empty.

slides.caption: Every element is equally likely to be picked.
Return a reference to that element.

note.text: result: always one of the 3: true

sample-slice.title: How IndexedRandom::sample works
sample-slice.description: Picks n different elements of a slice, at random.

slides.caption: No element is picked twice. Called choose_multiple before rand 0.10.
Ask for more than the length to get all.

choose-weighted.title: How IndexedRandom::choose_weighted works
choose-weighted.description: Picks one element, with chances set by a weight function.

slides.caption: Weights must not all be zero.
WeightedIndex is faster for repeated draws.

choose-mut.title: How IndexedMutRandom::choose_mut works
choose-mut.description: Picks one random element and gives you &mut to it.

shuffle.title: How SliceRandom::shuffle works
shuffle.description: Puts the elements of a slice in random order, in place.

slides.caption: Each position swaps with a random position at or before it, walking from the end.
Swap the last slot with a random slot.
Repeat towards the front. Nothing is added or lost.
Seed the rng (StdRng::seed_from_u64) to get the same order every run.

partial-shuffle.title: How SliceRandom::partial_shuffle works
partial-shuffle.description: Picks n random elements by shuffling only part of the slice.

slides.caption: Cheaper than shuffling everything when n is small.
sample() does it without changing the slice.

iter-choose.title: How IteratorRandom::choose works
iter-choose.description: Picks one random item of an iterator, without collecting it first.

slides.caption: Uses the size hint when it is exact; otherwise reservoir sampling.
choose_stable gives the same pick for the same seed even if the iterator changes how it hints its size.

iter-sample.title: How IteratorRandom::sample works
iter-sample.description: Collects n random items of an iterator into a Vec.

slides.caption: The order of the result is not random; shuffle it if that matters.

uniform-new.title: How Uniform::new works
uniform-new.description: A distribution that draws evenly from low..high.

slides.caption: Faster than random_range when drawing many values from one range.

distribution-sample-iter.title: How Distribution::sample_iter works
distribution-sample-iter.description: An endless iterator of samples, from the distribution's side.

slides.caption: The rng is borrowed for as long as the iterator lives.
RngExt::sample_iter is the same from the rng's side.

sample-string.title: How SampleString::sample_string works
sample-string.description: A random String of n characters from a distribution.

weighted-index-new.title: How WeightedIndex::new works
weighted-index-new.description: A distribution over indices with given weights.

note.text: index i with chance w[i] / total

slides.caption: Sampling gives an index; use it to look up the item. Building it once makes each draw fast.
Errors if the weights are empty, negative or all zero.

bernoulli-new.title: How Bernoulli::new works
bernoulli-new.description: A true/false distribution with probability p of true.

slides.caption: Errors if p is not in 0..=1.

index-sample.title: How rand::seq::index::sample works
index-sample.description: n distinct random indices out of 0..len.

slides.caption: Returns an IndexVec; iterate or into_vec().
Useful to pick from several parallel arrays.

from-seed.title: How StdRng::from_seed works
from-seed.description: A StdRng from a full 32-byte seed.

slides.caption: seed_from_u64 expands a u64 into such a seed for you.
Use the bytes as the state.
Keep the seed to replay a run.
